subject.title: fix(telegram): bound miniapp auth rate-limit map with sweep and cap

question: Is it acceptable for Mini App auth rate-limit state to evict the least-recently-used active IP at 1,024 keys, thereby restarting that IP's window under sustained distinct-IP pressure?
rationale: The implementation intentionally trades a bounded process-lifetime memory footprint for a documented fail-open reset on rare cap eviction; this is a security-boundary policy choice rather than a mechanical defect.

options.title: Accept bounded LRU eviction
options.body: Retain the 1,024-key cap and recency refresh because it bounds unauthenticated-route memory while preserving active-key protection until the cap is genuinely pressured.

options.title: Use a stricter limiter design
options.body: Replace cap eviction with a rate-limiter design that preserves denial state under cardinality pressure, accepting additional implementation and operational complexity.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded LRU eviction
recommendation.body: Retain the 1,024-key cap and recency refresh because it bounds unauthenticated-route memory while preserving active-key protection until the cap is genuinely pressured.
